rows.AI: RV only, CARMENES VIS. K_c=2.73 m/s (Sect. 4.2.3). Exists only in the two-circular-planets model, where b becomes circular with P=13.350 d and msini 15.58 M_E; in the preferred model b is single and eccentric (e=0.37) and there is no c. Horrobin & Rein 2019 also find 5:4 solutions (not tabulated here). TIER: Not an independent signal but an alternative reading of the one RV signal: the data fit either one eccentric planet (e=0.37) or two circular planets at 2:1. Horrobin & Rein 2019 show two-planet (2:1 or 5:4) fits are dynamically stable but do not choose. CARMENES DR1 (Ribas+2023) lists only the 13.35 d signal. exoplanet.eu nonetheless lists c as 'Confirmed'; NASA does not.

Drift slope 21.77+/-0.77 m/s/yr and curvature -11.62+/-0.77 m/s/yr^2 (Table 2, global fit; MCMC in Sect. 4 gives 21.1+/-2.8 m/s/yr and -10.3+/-2.4 m/s/yr^2); 2009 RVs ~8 m/s below 2010. TIER: Backed only by an RV trend (owner's ruling: still a candidate, ambiguous). The drift is strongly detected - 1 planet + quadratic drift beats 1 planet alone by a Bayes factor ~5e5 - and Mignon et al. 2025 again need a quadratic long-term term for GJ 3634's HARPS RVs, but no orbit, no period and no mass have been measured, and the nature (planet, brown dwarf or star) is unknown. rows.AI: Single TESS transit at 3471.566 (+0.009/-0.006) TBJD; Rp/R*=0.045+/-0.003, b=0.8 (+0.1/-0.2), T14=2.9 h (Table A.2). Period only bounded (>32.7 d from absence of other transits); median 74 d. Mass NOT measured: the authors estimate ~5.8+/-1.2 M_E from an empirical M-R relation (Muller et al. 2024), expected K 1-2.6 m/s. TESS Cycle 9 re-observation expected (sector 118). rows.AI: Circumbinary around RR Cae A (white dwarf) + B (M4). O-C amplitude 20 +/- 5 s, period 39 +/- 5 yr (Rattanamala et al. 2023 abstract). The eccentricity column of Table 8 did not extract cleanly from the PDF, so it is not reported. In the same two-object model the inner body (the sheet's RR Cae b) has P = 15.0 +/- 0.5 yr, 3.0 +/- 0.3 MJup, 5.2 au. TIER: Eclipse-timing (light-travel-time) inference from one O-C curve. Pulley et al. 2025 report new 2022-2025 timings that none of the recent RR Cae models fit, and note a Lanza-type magnetic mechanism is energetically possible for exactly this second modulation. ETV planets around post-common-envelope binaries have a poor record.
